questions.title: Logger Start End Decorator Drill
questions.description:
Decorator drill: wrap a function so the word start prints before it runs and the word end prints after.
The logger decorator wraps greet, which itself prints Hello, <name>.

Input Format:
One line: the name.

Output Format:
Line 1: start
Line 2: Hello, <name>
Line 3: end

Constraints:
The name is 1-80 characters

questions.title: Uppercase Return Decorator Drill
questions.description:
Decorator drill: transform the return value. The louden wrapper uppercases whatever the decorated shout function returns.
shout(msg) returns 'notice: ' + msg; the driver prints the decorated call's result.

Input Format:
One line: the message.

Output Format:
One line: NOTICE: <message uppercased>

Constraints:
The message is 1-80 characters

questions.title: Count Up Generator Drill
questions.description:
Generator drill: count_up(limit) yields the numbers 1..limit one at a time, and a for loop consumes them.

Input Format:
One integer: n.

Output Format:
The numbers 1..n, one per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50

questions.title: Genexpr Next Twice Drill
questions.description:
Generator expression drill: build (v * v for v in values) from the stdin values and pull exactly two values out with next().

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: square of the first value
Line 2: square of the second value

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 50; 0 <= value <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
values = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
squares = (v * v for v in values)
print(next(squares))
print(next(squares))

questions.title: Evens Only Filter Generator Drill
questions.description:
Lazy filter drill: evens_only(values) is a generator that yields only the even values, one per pass - nothing is collected up front.
The driver prints every yielded value.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
The even values, one per line, in input order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= value <= 1000; at least one value is even
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= value <= 1000; at least one value is even

questions.title: Countdown Generator Drill
questions.description:
Generator drill: countdown(start) yields start, start-1, ..., down to 1.

Input Format:
One integer: n.

Output Format:
The numbers n..1, one per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50

questions.title: Step Counter Decorator Lab
questions.description:
A build pipeline decorates each QA step with @step_counter, which remembers how many times it has run and prints call <k> before invoking the step; the step doubles its input and prints the result.
Read n values and run the step on each one.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
For each value: a line call <k> followed by a line with the doubled value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20; 0 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Rate Limiter Stub Decorator
questions.description:
An API gateway stub uses a decorator factory @rate_limiter(limit) to grant the first limit pings and block the rest.
The wrapper prints allowed and then calls ping (which returns pong <tag>), or prints blocked. The driver prints the returned greeting only for allowed calls.

Input Format:
Line 1: limit
Line 2: n
Next n lines: one tag each (single tokens).

Output Format:
Per call: allowed then pong <tag>, or just blocked.

Constraints:
1 <= limit <= 10; 1 <= n <= 20; tags are single tokens of 1-10 characters

questions.title: Sensor Batch Streamer
questions.description:
A telemetry bus streams sensor readings, and a generator batches(values, size) yields groups of at most <size> readings as they arrive - the final partial batch is still yielded.

Line 1: n and k.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line per batch: the batch's values space-separated.

1 <= k <= n <= 100

questions.title: Memoized Growth Forecaster
questions.description:
A power-grid forecaster answers repeated growth queries; a hand-rolled memo decorator caches results in a dict kept in its closure (no functools, no lru_cache).
growth(1) = growth(2) = 1 and growth(k) = growth(k-1) + growth(k-2).

Input Format:
Line 1: q
Next q lines: one k per line.

Output Format:
One line per query: growth(k).

Constraints:
1 <= q <= 10; 1 <= k <= 25

questions.title: Stock Tick Pipeline
questions.description:
A market-data desk builds a lazy three-stage generator pipeline: read_ticks yields ticks straight from stdin, above(stream, threshold) passes on only ticks strictly greater than the threshold, and scale(stream, factor) multiplies each surviving tick by the factor. The driver consumes the pipeline with a single for loop - no lists, no appends.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, threshold, factor.
Next n lines: one tick each.

Output Format:
One line per surviving tick: tick * factor.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; 0 <= threshold <= 1000000; 1 <= factor <= 100; 0 <= tick <= 1000000; at least one tick is above the threshold

questions.title: Thermal Audit Sum of Squares
questions.description:
A server-room audit scores thermal stress as the sum of squares of the abnormal readings - those that are even and positive - computed with a single generator expression feeding sum (no .append, no intermediate lists).

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line: the sum of squares of the even positive values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
values = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
total = sum(v * v for v in values if v % 2 == 0 and v > 0)
print(total)

questions.title: Stacked Decorator Order Probe

Input Format:

Next n lines: one amount each.

Output Format:
Five lines per amount, as described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10; 0 <= amount <= 10000

questions.title: Retry on Flaky Job Simulator
questions.description:
A deployment simulator retries a flaky job through a decorator factory @retry(limit). Each attempt prints attempt <k>. The wrapped job consults a deterministic schedule read from stdin (token 1 = succeed, token 0 = raise FlakyError); the wrapper catches FlakyError and prints failed. On success the wrapper prints success on attempt <k> and stops; if every allowed attempt fails it prints job aborted. Attempts beyond the schedule's length always fail, and schedule entries beyond the limit are never reached.
After a success the driver prints job done.

Input Format:
Line 1: limit
Line 2: the schedule, space-separated 0/1 tokens.

Output Format:
The attempt/failed/success trace as described, ending with job done or job aborted.

Constraints:
1 <= limit <= 10; 1 <= schedule length <= 10; tokens are 0 or 1

questions.title: ECG Running Stats Stream
questions.description:
A streaming ECG monitor exposes a generator that yields the tuple (index, running total, running maximum) after each sample, tracking the aggregates by hand (no sum(), no max(), no itertools). Samples may be negative, so the running maximum must be initialized from the first sample, not from zero.

Input Format:
Line 1: n
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line per sample: <index> <running total> <running max>.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; -10000 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
def running_stats(values):
    total = 0
    peak = None
    index = 0
    for v in values:
        index += 1
        total += v
        if peak is None or v > peak:
            peak = v
        yield (index, total, peak)


n = int(input())
values = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
for i, total, peak in running_stats(values):
    print(f"{i} {total} {peak}")

( records) - or (1 record) when the page holds a single record - then each record as two spaces, sku, space, qty. Constraints: 1 <= k <= 100; 1 <= n <= 500; 0 <= qty <= 1000; skus are 1-8 characters
